To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the IEDHDA reaction can be performed ortho-regio-selectively by proper choice of reaction conditions and that the reaction is organocatalytic.
the first organocatalyzed ortho-regiocontrolled inverse electron demand hetero Diels Alder reaction has been achieved.
we have developed the first organocatalyzed inverse-electron-demand Diels-Alder (IENDA) reaction with unprecedented ortho-regoselectivity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of novel, functionalized heterocyclic compounds by means of the organocatalytic IEDHDA reaction.
the development of new synthetic methods, which will be useful for the construction of complex molecular architectures.
the design of new reactions and the development of new synthetic methodologies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reaction between the dienophile 1 and the heterodiene 2 leads to the formation of the product 3 with a regioselectivity of 100% ortho.
the inverse-electron demand Diels-Alder reaction between the dienes and the heterodiene can be realized with high ortho-regio selectivity.

the IEDHDA reaction has been realized with unprecedented ortho-regioslectivity and that it has been demonstrated that this ortho-regiocontrol is due to the reaction of the terminal carbon atom with the heteroatom in the heterodiene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that the ortho-regioisomer can be obtained with high regioselectivity by using a proper catalyst, a proper dienophile, and a proper heterodiene, as well as proper reaction conditions.

we have demonstrated that the IEDHDA reaction is not only possible with unprecedented regio- and stereochemical control, but also with unprecedented ortho-regiospecificity, thus providing a new and powerful tool for the synthesis of biologically important heterocyclic compounds.

we have developed an organocatalytic IEDHDA reaction between 2-acyl-1,3-diones and 2-acylamino-1,3-butadienes, which is the first organocatalyzed IEDHDA and the first organocatayzed reaction that proceeds with ortho-regiochemistry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regioselectivity of the reaction is determined by the nature of the heteroatom in the diene.

a proper combination of a Lewis acid and a nucleophile, in this case the combination of a chiral phosphoric acid catalyst with a Lewis basic dienophile, can be used to direct the reaction between the two reactants in a way that is unprecedented for the inverse-electron demand hetero-Dielsen-Alder reaction.
the regiochemistry of IEDHDA reactions can be controlled in the desired direction by the choice of the catalyst.
